text: dsh-loop-engine 为 dsh web 提供按会话选择 agent 循环引擎的能力，可在内置 in-process 与 Claude Code、Codex、Pi、Kimi Code 之间分配会话。它通过单一路由 factory 将会话交给对应驱动，并提供设置页、聊天输入框切换器和会话引擎状态标记。用户可为新会话设默认引擎，也可在空闲会话中切换；托管引擎之间可原地换手，涉及内置循环时需重载页面。需要在主机安装并登录所选引擎的 CLI 或配置其所需凭据；具体配置取决于引擎。

dsh-loop-engine routes dsh web sessions to the built-in loop or Claude Code, Codex, Pi, and Kimi. It adds engine settings, a chat switcher, and status badge. Set a default or switch an idle session; hosted engines hand over in place, while moves involving the built-in loop reload the page.

我想在网页里给每个会话单独选择 agent 引擎。
dsh 能接入 Claude Code、Pi 这类本机编程 agent 吗？
给新建的 dsh 会话设置一个默认托管引擎。
怎么查看当前会话实际跑的是哪个 agent 引擎？
希望在聊天输入框里把空闲会话切换到另一种引擎。
I want different dsh sessions to use different coding agents.
Can I switch an idle chat between Codex, Pi, and Claude Code?
dsh-loop-engine 的功能「引擎路由」：根据会话记录和 preset 选择内置 in-process、Claude Code、Codex、Pi 或 Kimi 驱动；创建或恢复会话时由路由 factory 分发。
dsh-loop-engine 的功能「会话切换」：在聊天输入框的引擎选择器中为当前空闲会话切换引擎；托管引擎间原地换手，涉及 in-process 时先确认并重载页面。
dsh-loop-engine 的功能「新会话默认值」：在 Loop engine 设置页选择新会话默认使用的引擎；设置变更影响之后创建的会话，已有会话保留各自引擎。
dsh-loop-engine 的功能「会话引擎标记」：在会话标题区域显示当前会话实际使用的引擎，并可通过设置关闭标记；状态来自插件提供的会话引擎报告。

dsh-loop-engine README · dsh-loop-engine：Pick **dsh web**'s agent loop engine **per session** — the built-in `in-process` loop (the default), or one of the hosted engines `claude-code` / `codex` / `pi` / `kimi`. Sessions are independent: one chat can run Codex while another runs Kimi. Any open, idle session can move engines — between two hosted engines the handover is **in place**, and a move involving `in-process` **reloads the page** (the `dsh web` process never restarts). Nothing in the main repository changes.

dsh-loop-engine README · Install：```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-loop-engine
```

Boot `dsh web` once (the router retries for a bounded window while the base bundle still holds the agent-factory slot), then open **Settings → Loop engine**.

**Install notes**

dsh-loop-engine README · Install：- The install rewrites one **engine-agnostic** managed block in the profile's `cordis.patch.yml`; every other byte you wrote there is preserved. Upgrading from an older release needs no hand edit.
- **Installing into any profile but `web`** — the Desktop app's `desktop`, a `headless` deployment, a renamed profile — needs `profile: <name>` in the composition entry for that profile:
  ```yaml
  - id: loop-engine
    config:
      profile: desktop
  ```
  `profile` defaults to `web`, so without it the plugin writes its managed block into `<home>/profiles/web/cordis.patch.yml` while the running profile never reads it: the plugin mounts, but the base `agent-loop` row is never disabled, so its router cannot take the factory slot and no hosted engine is reachable. (Found by installing into the Desktop app.)
- **Uninstall** is `dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-loop-engine` **plus deleting that managed block** — the block outlives the plugin, and while it is present the profile has no agent factory, so no session can be created.
- **pnpm 10+** may block dependency build scripts (`ERR_PNPM_IGNORED_BUILDS`, naming `esbuild`, `@google/genai`, `protobufjs`).

dsh-loop-engine README · Requirements：| Engine | Needs, on the host |
|---|---|
| Claude Code | the Claude Code CLI installed and logged in |
| Codex | `codex login`, or a `CODEX_API_KEY` environment entry |
| Pi | whatever `pi` expects (its own `~/.pi/agent/auth.json`, or the provider's API-key variable) |
| Kimi Code | the `kimi` CLI installed and logged in, on `PATH` (or pinned via `kimiBin`) |

dsh-loop-engine README · Usage：- **New session** — pick the engine on the preset chip beside the workspace picker, or keep the deployment's default (`standard`) for the in-process loop. A child agent inherits its parent's engine.
- **Settings → Loop engine** sets the default for **new** sessions. It lands immediately; running sessions are unaffected. **In-process** restores whatever default the plugin replaced.
- **Move a session you are in** with the composer's engine selector (enable *Show the engine selector in the chat page*).
  - Hosted → hosted: in place, applies on the spot.
  - Anything involving `in-process`: the composer asks first, then the page reloads and reopens the same session (scroll position and unsent draft are lost; the record is not).
  - A mid-turn session is refused, and a subagent's session cannot be moved.
- **The header chip** beside the preset label names the engine the session on screen actually runs; *Show the engine badge in the conversation header* turns it off (and the header keeps no trace of the plugin).

dsh-loop-engine README · Version compatibility：One release serves the **0.1.5 line** (`>=0.1.5-rc.1 <0.1.6-0`), the **0.1.7 line** (`>=0.1.7-rc.1 <0.1.8-0`), the **0.2.0 line** (`>=0.2.0-rc.1 <0.2.1-0`) and the **0.2.1 line** (`>=0.2.1-rc.1 <0.2.2-0`): the plugin detects the running generation at load and takes the matching code path. Those union ranges are what it declares in `peerDependencies`, and a harness outside them fails loudly at boot or session resume.

dsh-loop-engine README · Version compatibility：Read the version as `<harness line>-rcN`, where **`rcN` is this plugin's own release counter for that line** — not the harness's `rc` number. Within a covered line a new harness `rc` needs no plugin release unless an API surface moved; [docs/compatibility.md](docs/compatibility.md) §1 lists those surfaces and the diff command that decides it.

dsh-loop-engine README · Version compatibility：`0.2.1-rc1` is the first release that serves four lines at once. Two harness changes force it: the 0.2.1 line **deleted `@deepseek-ai/dsh-invariants` and every `<package>/invariant` subpath**, and it republished the JSONL durability backend as a namespace plugin with no default export. The plugin's `./invariant` companion now declares the host registry's shape locally, so one build mounts on every line — and, because dsh skips a whole bundle whose `@deepseek-ai/dsh-*` peers do not satisfy the running version, dropping that package from `peerDependencies` is what lets the plugin load on 0.2.1 at all.

dsh-loop-engine README · Known limitations：- **It replaces the harness's agent factory.** One facade serves every session, so the plugin promises to stay out of the way: any session it cannot answer for — including sessions with nothing to do with hosted engines — degrades to the `in-process` loop instead of failing to open. See [docs/per-session-engine.md](docs/per-session-engine.md) §6.
- **The engine record is a sidecar**, `$DSH_HOME/.loop-engine/engines.json`, not part of the session log: changing machine or `DSH_HOME` loses it and the session falls back to its preset. See §5.5.
- **Moving a session involving `in-process` reloads the page** — the harness loop neither hands over a live session nor adopts one it did not create. See §5.2/§5.4.
- **Sessions that already ran a turn** can still move, but only while idle, and the move rebuilds that session's agent. See §5.
- **Old sessions with the legacy preset id `loop-engine`** read as "legacy hosted engine" until rebuilt once. See §7.
- **Same-engine sessions share that CLI's own auth directory**, with no lock added by the plugin. See §6.
